Thanks for the demo last week. Our privacy team has a couple of follow-ups before procurement can sign off on the DPA: two related items about data residency and short-term cross-region processing during initial seeding.

1) During onboarding, we expect a brief seeding window where a subset of our data will be ingested into Redwood in the US for dedup/normalization, after which customer data should be pinned to the EU region. 2) Which subprocessors (by name and region) may process data during that seeding window? We need roster-level visibility for our DPO.

Attached: DPO questionnaire (page 3 has the specific question set). Could you respond with the expected max window, any SLA or retention guarantees for the transient copy, and a subprocessor roster for the initial seeding?

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Irene (Privacy & Security) and Marissa (Customer Ops) who run onboarding.

High level answers up front: we support an explicit one-time seeding window of up to 72 hours for data migration/prefixing during onboarding, by default. We can contractually limit that to a shorter window (e.g., 24 or 48 hours) for an account with an addendum. During that window only the minimum operational tooling and a single small set of subprocessors will be engaged; non-essential analytics and broad telemetry are disabled.

Action items for us:
- Irene: can you confirm the subprocessor roster (names/regions) for the seeding flow and attach the runbook?

Dana — if 72 hours is too long we can tighten the window and include a DPA addendum clause that limits transient storage to X hours and requires a signed deletion confirmation from Redwood Ops.

Hi Dana, Jordan,

Thanks — putting the technical details here so legal has concrete language to reference. Attaching the seeding runbook and subprocessor roster.

Summary (technical):
- Default transient seed window: 72 hours (configurable per-account).
- Purpose: allow deduped model priming, KV prefix warm-up, and validation checks before pinning.
- Controls during window:
  • Only ingestion, normalization, and KV-store priming services run cross-region. Analytics and model telemetry pipelines are disabled by default.
  • KV caches created during seeding are marked as "transient" in metadata and are scheduled for automated deletion.
- Transient copy retention and verification:
  • After seeding completes, a two-step deletion is performed: (1) immediate logical delete and (2) background shred job to remove S3 objects and purge caches within 24 hours.
  • Ops produces a signed deletion manifest (sha256 + timestamps) that we can share or send to your security contact.
- Subprocessors involved (initial seeding only):
  • NimbusOps (US) — temporary data routing and normalization job (contracted subprocess)
  • EdgeCache-Partner (EU) — small cache pop during validation (EU-based nodes after the move)
  • AuditStore (US) — stores deletion manifests and operation logs (encrypted at rest)

We can provide a scoped addendum that:
- Restricts the seeding window to no more than 24/48/72 hours explicitly (you pick),
- Names the allowed subprocessors for the flow, and
- Commits to supply the signed deletion manifest within 48 hours of completion.

Attached: region-seed-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook, 18 pages), subprocessor_roster.csv (CSV)

Let me know if you want the language to be DPA-ready and we’ll draft the clause.
